newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA PARLIAMENT APPROVES PM'S RESIGNATION.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA PARLIAMENT APPROVES PM'S RESIGNATION.

text.p: Bulgaria's parliament on Saturday approved Prime Minister's Zhan Videnov resignation tendered at a party congress a week ago.
The resignation was accepted with 211 votes, three voted against and nine abstained from a total of 223 deputies.

Under fire for his handling of a severe economic crisis, Videnov resigned last Saturday, saying he felt he lacked the support he needed from the party and the country to continue as prime minister and party leader.

"I hope the Bulgarian people will not be punished for their patience by yet another government composed of former communists," opposition deputy and former prime minister Filip Dimitrov told parliament.
Dimitrov echoed calls of the opposition for early elections protesting against attempts of the Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP) to form a new cabinet.
Under the constitution the current cabinet remains in power until the ruling BSP composes a new cabinet which has to be approved by parliament next month.

Possible prime ministers include the speaker of parliament Blagovest Sendov, seen as a compromise candidate, and former foreign minister Georgi Pirinski, who resigned after a party confidence vote gave Videnov only narrow backing last month.
On Tuesday, the Socialist congress elected Georgi Parvanov as party leader, a choice seen as a compromise between party reformists and hardliners.

The BSP was formed by leading ex-communists who renamed the party after Zhivkov's overthrow in 1989. Its critics accuse it of being more interested in supporting its powerful business allies than in pushing through badly-needed economic reforms.

The opposition walked out during the vote of a second item under which the outgoing cabinet is expected to introduce to parliament the draft 1997 budget, a new privatisation law and legal amendments for the introduction of a currency board fixed exchange rate regime, allowing parliament to vote on them by mid-January.

"This government has shown that it is inept in drafting budgets and why should we burdened by yet another unrealistic budget after this cabinet is gone," opposition deputy Ventsisav Dimitrov told parliament.

Videnov's cabinet revised this year's budget three times to accomodate growing spending on domestic debt and subsidies to loss-making state enterprises. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569; 981 4145
